headline: ICE declares state laws 'shall not apply' to its private detention network
summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement is attempting to bypass state oversight for its private detention facilities, publishing draft contract terms that explicitly state state and local laws will not apply.
details: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is moving to place its private detention network beyond the reach of state inspectors. Draft contract terms published by ICE declare that state and local laws “shall not apply” to the facilities, according to federal documents.

This move follows a federal judge's ruling that a contract cannot override state law, ordering ICE’s largest Pacific Northwest detention center to open to Washington health officials. The ruling came after three years of litigation, 10 refused inspections, and 3,500 detainee complaints.

The judge found that the operator of Tacoma’s immigration detention center, GEO Group, could not use a new contract with ICE to override state law. ICE is now proposing to extend similar contract language, which attempts to nullify state law, to facilities in four regions of the country.

The procurement document, posted on July 10, suggests the contract terms align with four detention centers GEO already operates. Companies had less than a week to respond before the window closed July 17.

This strategy mirrors previous actions, such as in California, where a county was blocked from inspecting a detention center. The operator then sold the facility to DHS for $1.5 billion, which DHS tied to state politicians pushing legislation against private prisons.

topic: ocarina of time native ios port using ai
headline_marked: [[The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time]] gets native iOS port using AI
headline: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time gets native iOS port using AI
summary: Developer uses OpenAI's Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol to bring the N64 classic to iPhone and iPad, offering 60 FPS gameplay.
details: A developer has created HarkinianPad, a native port of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for iOS and iPadOS, leveraging AI tools like OpenAI's Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol. This allows the Nintendo 64 classic to run directly on Apple devices without emulation, offering modern features.

The port achieves smooth 60 FPS gameplay with widescreen and full-screen support, a significant upgrade from the original's 20 FPS and 240p resolution. HarkinianPad is built upon the Ship of Harkinian engine, an existing open-source project that decompiled the game into C code.

HarkinianPad utilizes Apple's Metal API for rendering, paving the way for higher native resolutions and enhanced performance. Users can opt for touch controls or connect a Bluetooth controller, mouse, or keyboard for a personalized gaming experience.

While not a traditional emulator, HarkinianPad requires users to possess a legally obtained ROM of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time to pull game assets. The project is freely available on GitHub, showcasing the power of AI in adapting community preservation efforts for new audiences.

This development comes as fans await Nintendo's official remake of Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2. The native iOS port demonstrates how AI coding tools can empower solo developers to bring retro titles to modern platforms.
